article_text:
‘I am lucky, as I have become old.” That is the pithy, personal summary offered by English film-maker David Wilkinson, whose previous movie was his thoughtful, eloquent film The Marbles , which reopened the case for the restitution of the Parthenon marbles to Greece. Now he reveals that he was in fact battling stage four bowel cancer throughout its making, and this new and very personal film is now about his own condition, a film in which the director is front and centre, speaking candidly to camera in the very midst of his treatment.

In fact, 1 in 2 is specifically about his shock and sadness that so many people alongside him in waiting rooms, or online in bowel cancer discussion groups are so young, in their 40s, or 30s, or 20s. Wilkinson makes it his business to give these people a voice, along with the medical professionals in the NHS who are battling to help them. He also wants to find something out: why is something that was once considered an old person’s disease on the rise in younger age groups in developed nations? It appears to be due to diet and lifestyle. Could it be microplastics? There are no clearcut answers.

This is a sobering but very compassionate, humorous, generous film, and one that shows how Wilkinson’s highly personal and unselfconsciously confessional style has grown into something very watchable and distinctive. He is the star of this film, but a more self-effacing star can hardly be imagined. It is not fashionable in documentary cinema for the film-maker’s voice and viewpoint to be so explicit, but Wilkinson has gone his own way – without a whole lot of help from the British film establishment – and made a real success of it.

Wilkinson’s interviews are revealing and moving; a young woman called Milli Tanner is particularly candid and courageous. Again and again, younger people with the disease report that they wasted precious time as a result of misdiagnosis – symptoms that would be urgently treated in older people are written off with the young. So Wilkinson is an evangelist for the bowel cancer test that you get through the post, and not to delay; the very English habits of avoidance and embarrassment can kill you. As for Mr Wilkinson himself, I hope to see another film from him soon.

Stars and scars: the art of Atong Atem at the NGV – in pictures

The National Gallery of Victoria presents the first major Australian solo exhibition of the Melbourne artist, whose work references African studio photography, family archives, Catholic imagery and science fiction, while paying tribute to the myths and traditions of Dinka Bor culture in South Sudan.

article_text:
Taika Waititi ’s Klara and the Sun , based on the book by Kazuo Ishiguro, stars Jenna Ortega as the titular robotic Artificial Friend.

The film follows Klara as she wishes for a charge or owner to claim her from the Friend Store, where she gets a limited amount of time in the front alcove to show off and garner attention. Then she is chosen by Josie (Mia Tharia), whose mother Chrissy ( Amy Adams ) is reluctant to purchase an older model of the product when the newer ones are being sold at Fancy Friends down the street. But Klara and Josie’s bond is solid from the moment they meet eye contact. Though Josie is “lifted,” or genetically enhanced, she is also gravely ill, and Klara does her best to cheer her up as well as her mother. The film also features Natasha Lyonne, Aran Murphy, Steve Buscemi and Rachel House.

"本展由该画廊的3位策展人能势阳子、福岛直、泷上华共同策划。跨越了当代艺术、建筑与时尚这几个策展人以往深耕的领域，展厅内汇聚了以“吃”“穿”“住”“排泄”等切近活动为起点、从多元视角探讨“与自然连结”这一主题的作品。参展艺术家共有10组：浅野友理子、板坂留五、今村文、岩名泰岳、加藤美佳、西条茜、铃木初音、台原蓉子、保良雄、山县良和。", "translated": true}, {"type": "展览标题“种与根”是为了让人联想到人类的迁移及其过程中的蜕变、身份认同与根基、创造之种如何扎根等视角而取的。能势在谈及寄托于展览的想法时表示：“如果仔细观看本展的作品，就会发现并非全都是美丽或可爱的植物。从中或许也能看到生命本身所包含的残酷性以及人类对自然环境的业障等。希望通过本次展览，能让大家在身处都市正中央的同时，也感受到人类同样是自然的一部分，并能以各种方式重新找回这种感知。”", {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本展整体结构营造出都市共同菜园或拥有多种植物的庭院的意象，分布在两个展厅中的各项作品既彼此松散连结，又共同构筑出一处风景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/8357109a/7ce3a46b-56c5-4c48-9a1c-05ad8a09f49f.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，今村文《温暖的家》", "排列在展厅中央呈筒状的毛线是台原蓉子的新作。台原以擅长制作地毯等工艺的簇绒（Tufting）地毯作品而闻名，她一直将年幼时从祖母那里学来的编织作为心灵的依托。在本展中，艺术家为了平复日常心情而编织的作品按月份整齐排列，长度与织目紧密程度的差异，表露出当时各异的心境。毛线用台原在生活中食用的洋葱皮染色，根据水煮的份量和时间会产生不同的色彩。作品标题标注了“某年某月”等各自的年月，在犹如日记般的作品中，个人的经验与自然的变化融为一体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/865e72b4/6472db96-c33c-4862-a513-a5aa4c96ae23.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，台原蓉子的作品。台原的地毯作品亦在第二展厅展出", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/7d2af156/b8eb4ea0-3054-430a-8009-8f6fba71621f.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，铃木初音的展示", Meadow》的装置。据称，毛茸茸的须山周围向上延伸至天花板的环状连结，寓意着与天堂某人的连结。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "本展将“与自然连结”置于核心主题，但其切入方式因艺术家而异。从房屋内部到故乡风景、日常食物与衣物、人们聚集的广场，再到福岛的土地，作品所面对的对象丰富多样。都市与乡村、过去与现在、人与人、人与自然。它们相互交织，让我们再次意识到我们每一个人也都是其中的一部分。本次展览将成为契机，引发我们去思考这种连结。", "translated": true}]

"text": "「行列」には古代から続く祝祭儀式の側面があるいっぽう、静かな服従や規律も思わせる。展示室では、戦地を想起させる、顔を覆われて横たわる人形の「列」が、仏教絵画の九相図に着想を得た骸骨のランウェイへとつながる。さらに、子供の誕生を祝福するつるし雛をモチーフにした衣装が上階へと伸び、生と死の循環が、続いていく行列を通して表現されている。"}, {"type": "image", Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "保良は前述の薄荷の作品《home》に加え、1時間に10分だけゲートが開くインスタレーション空間を制作した。福島のリサーチを続ける保良は、帰還困難区域でいまも一時帰宅というかたちでしか戻れない人々がいることを指摘し、「土地を奪われた人、奪われた原因はなんなのかをもう一度考えることができたら」と語る。中に入ってみると独特の香りが鼻を掠める。ガラスで覆われ触れることのできない土のブロックが足元に敷かれ、空間内には、絹糸や岩塩、大理石、溶岩石などが配置されている。明滅する電球、福島県大熊町で録音された鳥の声のリズムと連動する水滴、放射性物質の検査を経て蒸留された植物の一部など、異なる来歴や時間を持つ要素が共存し、静謐な空間を作り出す。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/43e5a90d/86b54d32-b36c-4488-84ed-e56a68f00c24.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "会場風景より、保良雄の展示。土のブロックは《still》", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「自然とのつながり」をテーマに据える本展だが、そのアプローチは作家によってじつに様々だ。家の内側から故郷の風景、日々の食べ物や衣服、人が集う広場、福島の土地まで、作品が向き合う対象は多岐にわたる。都市と農村、過去と現在、人と人、人と自然。それらが絡み合い、私たち一人ひとりもその一部であることに、あらためて気づかされる。本展は、そのつながりを考えるきっかけになるだろう。"}]

「食べる」「着る」「住む」「排泄する」といった身近な営みを出発点に

路傍や空き地、コンクリートの割れ目。都市の隙間には、自生する植物だけでなく、外来種や人工物と共存する生き物などが新しい生態系が作っている。異常気象や気候変動の影響が世界で広がり、人間の生活が自然環境を変える大きな要因となっているいま、自然と人工の境界は曖昧になりつつある。そんな現代の都市のなかで、私たちはいかにして自然とのつながりを取り戻せるのか。そうした問いを出発点としたグループ展 「種と根っこ―都市の耕し方」 が、 東京オペラシティ アートギャラリー で開幕した。会期は12月20日まで。

本展は、同ギャラリーの 能勢陽子、福島直、瀧上華 の3人のキュレーターによって企画された。現代美術、建築、ファッションと各キュレーターがこれまで携わってきた領域をまたぎ、会場には、「食べる」「着る」「住む」「排泄する」といった身近な営みを起点に、多様な視点で「自然とのつながり」というテーマを扱った作品が集う。参加アーティストは、 浅野友理⼦、板坂留五、今村⽂、岩名泰岳、加藤美佳、⻄條茜、鈴⽊初⾳、䑓原蓉⼦、保良雄、⼭縣良和 の10組。

タイトルの「種と根っこ」は、人間の移動やその過程における変容、アイデンティティやルーツ、創造の種がどのように根付くのか、といった視点につながるものとしてつけられた。能勢は 「本展の作品をよく見ていただくと、かならずしも美しかったり、かわいらしかったりする植物ばかりではない。そこには、生命がそもそもはらんでいる残酷さや自然環境に対する人間の業なども見えてくるのではないかと思う。本展を通して、都市のただなかにいながら、人間も自然の一部であり、様々なやり方でその感覚を取り戻せるということを感じてもらえたら」 と展覧会に込めた思いを述べた。

ここでは会場を巡りながら各作家の主な作品を紹介する。

絡み合う植物や生命、変わりゆく風景

展覧会は展示室の外から始まっている。入り口付近に置かれた、植物のプランターと家具が一体化した椅子は保良雄の作品で、中には薄荷が植えられている。会場内にもそれぞれ種類の異なる和薄荷と改良品種が点在し、人間が様々な動機で作り変えてきた植物の変化を映し出す。

本展では、展覧会全体が都市の共同菜園や多様な種類の植物がある庭をイメージした構成になっており、ふたつの展示室に広がるそれぞれの作品は、ゆるやかにつながりながらひとつの風景をかたち作る。

最初の展示室内に足を踏み入れ、まず目に入るのは、今村文による赤い花の作品群だ。壁一面に貼られた35点の《温かい家》の植物のかたちは、どこか心臓や肺、血管など人体を思わせる。これらはすべて架空の花で、作家は水彩画をコラージュして異なるイメージを作り上げている。今回はこの「家」が外につながっていくイメージで、「裏庭」となる新作インスタレーションも制作した。平面作品の《赤い花ふたつ》では、隣合って根や枝葉が絡み合う植物の姿に、目には見えない人と人との関係性を重ねている。

浅野友理子は、東京オペラシティの植栽を管理する造園家への取材をもとに、絵画《落果の営み》を描いた。実が落ちて地面を汚すため早めに剪定されてしまうヤマモモは、「山のおやつ」として食べられてきたものでもある。そこに都市におけるひとつの自然の在り方を見た作家は、アスファルトに落ちるはずだったヤマモモの染みを、共生関係にあるイヌビワとコバチや、都市で出会った虫とともに生き生きと描き出した。自身で育てた植物や記憶の中の植物がひとつの庭を形成する《綯い交ぜの庭》でも、草花や虫、人間が絡み合う自然のネットワークを感じさせる。

岩名泰岳は、過疎化が進む故郷の三重県島ヶ原に暮らし、土地や暮らしの変容をめぐる絵画を制作してきた。今回は2020年代以降の絵画とドローイングを中心に展示。描かれているのは、空き家になって倒壊した家の柱や、道端の野仏、墓石のような丸い石など、作家が日々の生活で目にしたものや、人々の記憶の中にある風景だが、それらはシンプルな形態へと抽象化されている。そこには故郷の景色が変化するなかで風景が抽象化されていくようにも感じたという作家の感覚が反映されている。作家は、場所に残る痕跡や時間の移り変わりを絵画でとらえたい、と話す。

2026年に制作された《浄土》では、村の外れにある廃棄物処理場の光景に着想を得た。人が出したゴミから堆肥が作られる際に立ち上る湯気に人魂のイメージを重ね、再生と循環をテーマに描いている。

生活と地続きの創作、暮らしの中にある素材

より身近で個人的な日々の営みへ目を向け、素材そのものを暮らしのなかに見出す作家たちもいる。

展示室中央に並ぶ筒状の毛糸は䑓原蓉子の新作だ。絨毯制作などに用いるタフティングによるラグ作品で知られる䑓原は、幼い頃に祖母に教わった編み物を心の拠り所としてきた。本展では、作家が日々気持ちを落ち着かせるために編んだものが月ごとにまとめて並べられており、長さや編目の詰まり具合の違いに、その時々の心の状態が表れている。毛糸は生活のなかで䑓原が食した玉ねぎの皮で染められ、煮出す量や時間によって色の違いが生まれる。タイトルには「何年何月」とその時々の年月がつけられており、日記のような作品のなかに、個人的な経験と自然の変化が溶け合っている。

小部屋に並ぶ鈴木初音の作品も、素材が作家の生活とつながっている。鈴木の作品では、自身が食べるために植えた菊芋の茎を漉いて作った支持体に、はんだごてで焦げ目をつけて描いた変形の平面作品や、旅先で食べた牡蠣の貝殻に着想し、貝殻を焼成して作った石灰モルタルを引っ掻いて描いた作品など、自身の生活のなかの出来事と創作が直接的に結びついている。鈴木はこうした手法を通して「私が生きていることと絵を描くことが地続きになっていることを体感できる」と話す。今回は、様々な生き物が生きる水辺をイメージした作品群が並び、壁にも水面に広がる波紋のような絵が描かれている。

加藤美佳が素材にしたのは、とうもろこしの芯やひげなど、家庭から出て捨てられてしまうような小さく儚いものたちだ。「人間が戦争をやめられたらいいと思っている」と話す加藤のなかには、日常へのまなざしと遠く離れた場所への想像力が共存する。今回は、荒廃した世界で取り残され、有り合わせのものをおもちゃにして遊ぶ子供たちに寄り添いたいとの思いから素材を見つめ直し、《Grandma, Grandma, I'm Making a Meadow》と題したインスタレーションを制作した。ふわふわとしたひげの山の周囲から天井へと伸びる輪のつらなりは、天国の誰かとつながるイメージだという。

行列、広場、水。人と人、異なる要素が集まる場所

ふたつ目の展示室では、人が集まる場や共同の営みへと視点が広がる。

一際目を引くのは、ファッションデザイナー・山縣良和による骸骨のランウェイだ。山縣は、子供がトイレの前に人形を並べて遊ぶ光景に着想を得て、人間の根源的な営みとしての「行列」をテーマにしたインスタレーションを制作した。現在開催中の 「第一回前橋国際芸術祭2026」 で発表している作品のコンセプトを引き継ぐ本作は、展示室外の廊下から彫刻や玩具などが並び、子供から大人へと成長する過程が表現される。「学び」の行列の先には、山縣が主宰するcoconogaccoの学生の作品も並ぶ。

「行列」には古代から続く祝祭儀式の側面があるいっぽう、静かな服従や規律も思わせる。展示室では、戦地を想起させる、顔を覆われて横たわる人形の「列」が、仏教絵画の九相図に着想を得た骸骨のランウェイへとつながる。さらに、子供の誕生を祝福するつるし雛をモチーフにした衣装が上階へと伸び、生と死の循環が、続いていく行列を通して表現されている。

行列の向こうには、建築家の板坂留五が「広場」のような集いの場を作った。「普段とアウトプットは異なるが、頭や手の使い方、周囲に応答するような作り方は近い」と板坂。レンガのようなブロックは、同ギャラリーの前回展 「ほぼ、空：青木淳 ＋ リチャード・タトル」 で使われた発泡スチロールを切って再利用したものだ。状況に応じて、来場者がここから作品を鑑賞したり、トークイベントが開催されたりする場になるという。さらに板坂は、音楽家の櫂快太郎と協働し、30分に1回音を発する作品も制作した。鐘の音や声などのサウンドが時報のように流れ、展示室内の時間の動きを可視化する。

奥で強い存在感を放つのは、西條茜の大きな陶作品だ。手捻りによって作家の身体感覚の痕跡を残した独特の造形は、釉薬の色彩や質感、形態がどこか人間の臓器を思わせる。本展では大きな急須のようなかたちや畝のようなかたちなど、「水」の要素を伴う新作を制作。内部に湛えた水を、隣にある保良雄の薄荷の苗に注ぐパフォーマンスも行われ、その様子が映像で紹介されている。集団で水を注ぐ行為は儀式的であると同時に日常的な労働でもある。西條は人々がともに作業し休む、コミュニティのような場をイメージしてこの空間を構想したという。

保良は前述の薄荷の作品《home》に加え、1時間に10分だけゲートが開くインスタレーション空間を制作した。福島のリサーチを続ける保良は、帰還困難区域でいまも一時帰宅というかたちでしか戻れない人々がいることを指摘し、「土地を奪われた人、奪われた原因はなんなのかをもう一度考えることができたら」と語る。中に入ってみると独特の香りが鼻を掠める。ガラスで覆われ触れることのできない土のブロックが足元に敷かれ、空間内には、絹糸や岩塩、大理石、溶岩石などが配置されている。明滅する電球、福島県大熊町で録音された鳥の声のリズムと連動する水滴、放射性物質の検査を経て蒸留された植物の一部など、異なる来歴や時間を持つ要素が共存し、静謐な空間を作り出す。

「自然とのつながり」をテーマに据える本展だが、そのアプローチは作家によってじつに様々だ。家の内側から故郷の風景、日々の食べ物や衣服、人が集う広場、福島の土地まで、作品が向き合う対象は多岐にわたる。都市と農村、過去と現在、人と人、人と自然。それらが絡み合い、私たち一人ひとりもその一部であることに、あらためて気づかされる。本展は、そのつながりを考えるきっかけになるだろう。

article_text:
As Beatles fans are transported back to Abbey Road for Sam Mendes ‘ upcoming biopic, Paul McCartney has some thoughts on the casting.

The Beatles alum said he was concerned that Paul Mescal looks “markedly shorter” compared to his co-stars, and he even reached out to Mendes about it, but doesn’t know how the director is “gonna deal with it” in the four-film cinematic event.

“Yeah, and guess what? He’s smaller than the guy who’s playing John [Lennon],” explained McCartney on the Good Hang with Amy Poehler podcast. “Sam Mendes is making the film. I heard Sam Mendes is making the film. I said, ‘Sam, I’ve got just one thing that I need to say to you. Paul’s a bit smaller.'”

Related Stories

Sam Mendes’ Beatles Biopic Recreates ‘Abbey Road’ Album Cover In Behind-The-Scenes Video — Watch

Everything We Know About Sam Mendes’ Beatles Biopics So Far

After the movies’ cast re-created the iconic Abbey Road (1969) album cover while filming in London back in August, McCartney said his concerns worsened.

Watch on Deadline

“So, I don’t know how Sam’s gonna deal with it, but he sent me a picture, a still from the filming they were doing,” he recalled. “They were crossing the Abbey Road crossing, and the Paul character is markedly smaller.”

McCartney continued, “So, I texted him, ‘Sam! Smaller! Don’t do this! You said you wouldn’t do it.’ He said, ‘No, it’s ok. It’s just the stride.’ And he sent me another one where they were equal.”

Last February, Deadline exclusively revealed that Mendes is set to direct each installment of The Beatles — A Four-Film Cinematic Event , through his Neal Street Productions and Sony Pictures Entertainment. Each film will connect, telling the band’s story from each member’s point of view.

The film has since cast Mescal as Paul McCartney, Joseph Quinn as George Harrison, Barry Keoghan as Ringo Starr and Harris Dickinson as John Lennon.

article_text:
Ha quasi cinquemila anni e potrebbe riscrivere un capitolo della storia della navigazione nel Mediterraneo. In Turchia , al largo dell’isola di Kekova, nella provincia di Antalya, un gruppo di archeologi ha individuato quello che viene indicato come il più antico relitto navale finora conosciuto : una piccola imbarcazione commerciale dell’Età del Bronzo Antico, databile approssimativamente tra 4.400 e 4.700 anni fa.

Del legno della nave non rimane praticamente nulla. A consentire la datazione sono soprattutto le oltre 30 grandi giare da trasporto rinvenute sul fondale, insieme a tre ancore di pietra. Il sito si trova a circa 30 metri di profondità, su un terreno in parte sabbioso e in parte roccioso, nei pressi di una costa che per millenni ha rappresentato un passaggio importante lungo le rotte del Mediterraneo orientale.

Le anfore come indizio per datare il relitto

Il sito era stato documentato nel 2024 durante una campagna condotta dall’Akdeniz University sotto la direzione dell’archeologo subacqueo Hakan Öniz . Un primo rapporto scientifico, firmato da Öniz insieme a Ceyda Öztosun e pubblicato nel luglio 2026 sul Journal of Maritime Archaeology , ha ricondotto il carico all’Età del Bronzo Antico sulla base delle caratteristiche delle ceramiche.

Le anfore presentano infatti elementi confrontabili con recipienti provenienti dal Levante: manici laterali, basi piatte, decorazioni incise e forme documentate in diversi siti del Mediterraneo orientale. Analisi successive hanno indicato per alcuni esemplari possibili collegamenti con produzioni dell’area della Valle del Giordano, mentre recipienti simili sono stati rinvenuti anche in Egitto, nell’area di Troia e a Creta.

L’assenza dello scafo impedisce di ricorrere direttamente alla datazione al radiocarbonio del legno. È quindi soprattutto il confronto tipologico e tecnologico delle ceramiche a collocare il naufragio intorno alla metà del III millennio a.C., nello stesso ampio periodo storico in cui in Egitto venivano costruite le grandi piramidi di Giza.

Che cosa trasportava la nave?

Anche il contenuto delle giare potrebbe fornire nuove informazioni sulle reti commerciali di quasi cinque millenni fa. Alcuni recipienti conservano ancora residui visibili, oggi sottoposti ad analisi. Tra le ipotesi ci sono olio d’oliva, vino e resine vegetali, merci che potevano essere trasportate lungo le rotte tra Levante, Anatolia, Egeo ed Egitto.

Particolare attenzione è stata riservata a un recipiente caratterizzato da nove segni e due fori nel corpo. Secondo una prima interpretazione, potrebbe essere stato utilizzato anche nella lavorazione di prodotti caseari, forse per produrre burro o formaggio durante la navigazione. Si tratta, tuttavia, di un’ipotesi ancora da approfondire.

Intorno al carico sono state individuate inoltre due ancore in pietra a tre fori e un’altra a foro singolo. Il rapporto scientifico invita alla cautela: non è ancora possibile stabilire con certezza se tutte appartenessero all’imbarcazione. Le loro tipologie trovano però confronti in contesti dell’Età del Bronzo minoici, ciprioti, anatolici e levantini.

Una rotta tra il Levante, Troia e Creta

Le informazioni raccolte finora suggeriscono che si trattasse di una piccola nave impegnata in una navigazione da est verso ovest. I ricercatori ipotizzano una partenza dalle coste levantine e una possibile destinazione verso l’Anatolia nord-occidentale, nell’area di Troia, oppure verso la Creta minoica. La rotta precisa resta però ancora da dimostrare.

Il carico offre una preziosa testimonianza materiale dell’esistenza di collegamenti marittimi a lunga distanza nel Mediterraneo orientale durante l’Età del Bronzo Antico, quando merci, tecnologie e modelli culturali già circolavano tra regioni molto distanti. Le prossime indagini potrebbero chiarire la provenienza esatta delle ceramiche, il contenuto delle giare e la rotta seguita dall’imbarcazione.

Il nuovo primato dell’archeologia subacquea

Se la datazione sarà ulteriormente confermata dalle prossime analisi, il relitto di Kekova supererebbe quello individuato presso l’isola greca di Dokos, risalente a circa 4.200 anni fa e finora generalmente considerato il più antico relitto conosciuto. Diverso è invece il primato del più antico relitto con lo scafo ancora conservato, attribuito alla nave di circa 2.400 anni fa rinvenuta nelle acque anossiche del Mar Nero.

I reperti recuperati a Kekova sono ora sottoposti a conservazione e studio. Secondo quanto annunciato dal Ministero turco della Cultura e del Turismo, una parte dei materiali dovrebbe essere esposta nel nuovo museo dedicato all’archeologia subacquea del Mediterraneo ad Antalya.

Italia e Turchia rafforzano la cooperazione archeologica

Proprio in questi giorni, nella cornice del sito di Hierapolis, in Anatolia, il Ministro della Cultura italiano Alessandro Giuli e il Ministro della Cultura e del Turismo turco Mehmet Nuri Ersoy hanno inaugurato il XVII Convegno di Archeologia dedicato al contributo delle missioni archeologiche italiane attive nel Paese.

«Italia e Turchia condividono una storia millenaria che è una responsabilità viva verso il futuro. La cooperazione archeologica è una forma concreta di diplomazia culturale che pratica quotidianamente l’amicizia tra Italia e Turchia attraverso la condivisione dei metodi, il rispetto delle competenze, la tutela dei siti e la trasmissione del sapere alle nuove generazioni», ha dichiarato Giuli.

L’iniziativa, organizzata dall’Istituto Italiano di Cultura di Istanbul con il sostegno dell’Ambasciata d’Italia ad Ankara, coinvolge quindici missioni italo-turche impegnate nella ricerca e nella tutela del patrimonio archeologico anatolico.

A margine dell’incontro, Giuli ed Ersoy hanno discusso anche dei risultati della collaborazione culturale tra i due Paesi, a partire dalla mostra Troia e Roma. Miti, leggende, storie del Mediterraneo antico al Parco Archeologico del Colosseo. Tra le nuove iniziative concordate figurano inoltre l’avvio di un gemellaggio tra il Parco Archeologico di Pompei e quello di Efeso e un intervento congiunto di valorizzazione del sito di Elaiussa Sebaste, in Cilicia, con il coinvolgimento dell’Istituto Centrale di Archeologia.

"因此，结尾具有了象征性重回根源的意义。在四处探寻自己的道路之后，皮诺·丹尼尔在自己的城市里重新找到了能够让其音乐在保持通用语言的同时得以完全实现的归宿。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Dietro il successo di un artista possono nascondersi inquietudini profonde, legami irrisolti e il bisogno costante di trovare una propria identità. È su questo terreno che si sviluppa Je so’ pazzo , il film diretto da Nicola Prosatore , presentato alla Festa del Cinema di Roma nella sezione Grand Public e arrivato contemporaneamente nelle sale. Prodotta da Rai Cinema e distribuita da 01 Distribution, la pellicola ripercorre gli anni decisivi della vita di Pino Daniele , soffermandosi sulle esperienze che hanno contribuito a formare l’uomo prima ancora del musicista.

A interpretarlo è Massimiliano Caiazzo , conosciuto dal pubblico per il ruolo nella serie Mare Fuori . L’attore si è preparato a lungo, studiando chitarra e canto e affrontando una trasformazione fisica per avvicinarsi al personaggio. Un impegno che si confronta con la complessità di una figura ancora profondamente radicata nella memoria collettiva italiana. Liberamente ispirato al libro Pino Daniele. « Tutto quello che mi ha dato emozione viene alla luce» , scritto dal figlio Alessandro , il film porta la firma di Nicola Prosatore anche nella sceneggiatura, realizzata insieme ad Alessandro Daniele e Edoardo Puma .

L’intento è allontanarsi dall’immagine consacrata dell’artista per riscoprirne le origini, seguendo il passaggio dal ragazzo Pinotto al cantautore destinato a lasciare un segno nella musica contemporanea. L’infanzia difficile e il rapporto tormentato con il padre rappresentano una componente essenziale di questo percorso. La musica diventa progressivamente uno spazio di libertà, il luogo in cui dare forma a emozioni che faticano a trovare espressione nella vita quotidiana. La ricerca artistica si intreccia così con quella affettiva, in un continuo confronto con le proprie fragilità.

Anche Napoli occupa una posizione centrale nel racconto. La città che emerge dalla pellicola non è quella rassicurante delle immagini da cartolina, ma un organismo complesso, attraversato da disuguaglianze, contraddizioni e desideri di riscatto. Daniele ne raccoglie le voci senza indulgere nel folklore, costruendo una musica capace di fondere blues, jazz e tradizione partenopea in una sintesi originale. Il risultato è un linguaggio che supera i confini locali senza perdere il legame con il territorio d’origine.

Il titolo del film Je so’ pazzo è la chiave di lettura dell’intero film . Riprende il nome dell’album pubblicato nel 1979, ne evidenzia la tensione verso l’indipendenza e la ribellione, richiamando idealmente la figura di Masaniello che trasforma la libertà individuale in una presa di posizione collettiva. Quella che sembra una dichiarazione provocatoria diventa manifesto di un artista insofferente alle convenzioni, deciso a seguire la propria strada anche a costo di scontrarsi con le aspettative degli altri.

L’affermazione professionale non risolve tuttavia il conflitto con le proprie radici. Allontanarsi da Napoli diventa una necessità per crescere, ma anche una scelta vissuta con sofferenza, quasi fosse una rinuncia a una parte di sé. La distanza finisce per rivelare quanto la città sia profondamente intrecciata alla sua identità.

Il racconto culmina nel concerto del 1981 in Piazza del Plebiscito, davanti a oltre 200.000 persone. Quell’evento rappresenta il punto d’incontro tra la storia personale del musicista e quella di una comunità che nella sua voce riconosce la propria anima.

Il finale assume così il significato di un ritorno simbolico alle origini. Dopo aver cercato altrove la propria strada, Pino Daniele ritrova nella sua città il luogo in cui la propria musica può compiersi pienamente mantenendo un linguaggio universale.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Spin Wars , a documentary about the billion-dollar boutique fitness revolution, has landed a buyer.

Greenwich Entertainment has acquired the North American distribution rights to the doc, which marks the directorial debut of Philip Byron , the former SpringHill Entertainment unscripted chief who is now head of original content at Tom Brady’s Shadow Lion.

The film had its world premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival and recently played at the Hamptons International Film Festival.

It tells the story of SoulCycle, Flywheel, Peloton and centers around Ruth Zukerman, co-founder, SoulCycle and Flywheel Sports, and Marion Roaman, co-founder, Peloton, often referred to as the godmothers of New York’s indoor cycling scene. It features the likes of Katie Couric, Heather McMahan, Mary Beth Barone, Jill Kargman, Anna Roisman and Brandon Kyle Goodman.

Related Stories

Kōji Fukada's Cannes Competition Title 'Nagi Notes' Scores North American Deal With Greenwich Entertainment

Sundance Dark Comedy 'Run Amok' Gets North American Deal With Greenwich Entertainment

Greenwich will release the film in December.

Watch on Deadline

Spin Wars comes from Feed the Animals and Fulwell Entertainment, was produced by Byron and Jillian A.G., and written by Byron and James Thayer. Executive producers include Thayer, Stevenson Waite, Naomi Wright, Jamal Henderson, Luke Anderson and Amanda Goldfine.

“ Spin Wars has always been a passion project in every sense of the word. I started taking spin classes in New York City back in 2010 and had no idea about the juicy stories unfolding behind the scenes,” Byron said. “Whether you love or hate group fitness, this documentary has something for you. The world and the people in it are incredibly captivating and entertaining. It’s like The Social Network and Desperate Housewives got married, with Lady Gaga or Kesha officiating. I’m thrilled that Greenwich will bring the film to audiences so they can take the ride. Lots of gratitude to Feed the Animals and Fulwell for their partnership and support, and to all of our subjects for generously sharing their time and experiences with us.”

editorial_title_zh: 访谈：皮特罗·马切罗谈《杜丝》
editorial_excerpt_zh: 恩典状态：这位意大利作者导演探讨了他的最新作品，一部关于20世纪初著名舞台剧女演员的肖像片
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "埃莱奥诺拉·杜丝是第一位登上《时代》杂志封面的演员，也是第一位登上该封面的意大利人。1923年7月30日的那期杂志，是为了记录这位年满64岁、被广泛认为是世界最优秀表演艺术家之一的舞台剧女演员的美国巡演归来。查理·卓别林称她为“我见过最伟大的艺术家”，剧作家乔治·萧伯纳则以偏爱她而非长期竞争对手萨拉·伯恩哈特而闻名。1924年她逝世后，《纽约时报》的一篇赞誉文章写道：“杜丝艺术的主要部分在于一种无人能确切看到或充分描述的事物——一种我们只能用‘精神’这个贫乏、陈腐的词来指代的事物。”该作者接着指出：“或许杜丝力量的秘密在于她的眼睛，它们总是明亮的，却似乎总是对外部世界视而不见，其光芒完全发自内心。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "杜丝的方法比同时代人更具内在性与自然主义色彩，启发了演员工作室导演李·斯特拉斯堡，安娜·马尼亚尼和玛丽莲·梦露也是她的崇拜者，尽管她们只能通过二手资料来阅读和了解她的作品。她的表演似乎天生就是为电影而生的，但她始终献身于戏剧，仅出演过一部电影——1917年的影片《灰烬》（Cenere），尽管她对此不以为然，但其中仍流露出她那克制的张力。", "links": [{"text": "Cenere", "url": "https://filmcomment.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=bea725f8e0ef56b82be4ae760&id=f5b59c7ac6&e=270138fa20"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "皮特罗·马切罗的光辉新作《杜丝》摒弃了标准传记片中那种兴衰起伏的套路，浸润在被第一次世界大战满目疮痍的意大利那消逝的魅力之中。马切罗没有聚焦于这位女演员的众多辉煌成就，而是着墨于她晚年的挣扎与屡次失败。延续了他作品中精致美感与粗粝、纪录片式即兴感的对位融合——包括《迷失与美》（2015）、《马丁·伊登》（2019）和《红》（2022）——《杜丝》因瓦莱里娅·布鲁尼·特德斯基对杜丝那光芒四射、仿佛被附体般的表演而得到了宏大的支撑：即便在最私密的时刻，她也是一个舞台上的女性，她的一举一动都意味深长。特德斯基富有表现力的眼睛暗示了杜丝动荡的内心生活，此时她正试图在一个法西斯主义正不断崛起的世道中，为自己和艺术找到一席之地。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "杜丝拒绝被婚姻（她与演员特巴尔多·切奇的结合并未持续多久，她与剧作家加布里埃莱·邓南津的关系也十分动荡）或母亲的责任（她将女儿送去了寄宿学校）所束缚，她是一位艺术家和叛逆者，这使她成为马切罗的契合题材。我在9月份于多伦多国际电影节举办该片的北美首映后采访了他。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "瓦莱里娅·布鲁尼·特德斯基对埃莱奥诺拉·杜丝的演绎堪称卓越。与她合作是怎样的体验？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "可以说，我是在一种恩典状态下完成这部电影的。瓦莱里娅不仅是一位伟大的演员，也是一位伟大的导演，这带来了极大的助力。我们两人都很热爱即兴创作。我出身于纪录片领域，因此即兴对我而言是一种至关重要的力量。片中的许多场景都是我亲自掌镜拍摄的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你拍摄瓦莱里娅的方式确实给人一种真实电影（cinema verité）的感觉。你捕捉到了她的反应，而片中许多重要内容都蕴含在她所说的话与她真实感受之间的差异之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "手持摄影机是一种对位手段。保持对比非常重要——不能让影片显得过于古典，或者像一部标准的传记片。要让我去拍那种类型的电影会很困难！对我而言，与她建立直接的关系至关重要，这也是为什么我需要亲自操作摄影机并快速移动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在构筑表演方面，几乎没有任何现存的杜丝影像资料，这是否是一个挑战？", "爱迪生曾留下过一段录音，但后来遗失了。还有她与女儿恩里凯塔[在片中由诺埃米·梅兰饰演]之间的书信。恩里凯塔非常笃信宗教，她的儿子们后来都成了神父。至于瓦莱里娅如何塑造埃莱奥诺拉，对我来说关键在于寻找她的精神内核。我并不对声名鹊起的历程感兴趣；我感兴趣的是她晚年脆弱不堪的最后几年，以及当时国家的瓦解。那正是我想要描绘的处境。", "translated": true}, {"type": article_text:
Eleonora Duse was the first actor—and the first Italian—to appear on the cover of Time Magazine. The occasion, for the July 30, 1923 edition, was an American comeback tour by the 64-year-old stage actress who was widely considered one of the world’s finest performers. Charlie Chaplin called her “the greatest artist I have ever seen,” and playwright George Bernard Shaw famously preferred her to longtime rival Sarah Bernhardt. A New York Times appreciation after her death in 1924 said that “the major part of Duse’s art lay in a thing which no one could definitely see or adequately describe—the thing for which we have only the poor, hackneyed word ‘spirit.’” The writer went on to suggest that “perhaps the secret of Duse’s power lay in her eyes, which, always luminous, seemed always blind to the outward world, taking their light from within.”

Duse’s approach, more internal and naturalistic than her contemporaries, inspired Actors Studio director Lee Strasberg, and her fans included Anna Magnani and Marilyn Monroe, even though they could only read and hear about her work secondhand. Her acting seems tailor-made for cinema, but she remained devoted to theater and appeared in just one movie, the 1917 film Cenere (“Ashes”), which, though she dismissed it, offers glimpses of her controlled intensity.

Eschewing the rise-and-fall tropes of the standard biopic, Pietro Marcello’s lustrous Duse is bathed in the fading glamour of an Italy ravaged by the First World War. Instead of focusing on the actress’s many triumphs, Marcello hones in on the struggles and frequent failures of her later years. With the contrapuntal blend of exquisite beauty and raw, documentary-style immediacy that characterizes his films—including Lost and Beautiful (2015), Martin Eden (2019), and Scarlet (2022)— Duse is magnificently anchored by Valeria Bruni Tedeschi’s radiant, seemingly possessed performance as Duse: a woman of the stage even in her most private moments, her every gesture speaking volumes. Tedeschi’s expressive eyes suggest Duse’s turbulent inner life, as she tries to find a place for herself and her art in a world in which fascism is on the rise.

Refusing to be bound by marriage (her union with actor Tebaldo Checchi did not last long, and she had a turbulent relationship with the playwright Gabriele D’Annunzio) or the demands of motherhood (she sent her daughter away to boarding school), Duse was an artist and a rebel, making her a fitting subject for Marcello. I talked to him just after the film ’s North American premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.

Valeria Bruni Tedeschi gives an extraordinary performance as Eleonora Duse. What was it like collaborating with her?

I can say that I did this movie in a state of grace. Valeria is a great actress but also a great director, and that contributed a lot. Both of us love improvisation. I come from documentary, so for me improvisation is a vital force. I operated the camera for many of the scenes.

The way you film Valeria does feel like cinema verité . You catch her reactions, and a lot of what is important in the film is in the difference between what she’s saying and what she’s really feeling.

The handheld camera was a counterpoint. It was important for there to be contrast—not to have the film feel too classical, or like a standard biopic. It would have been difficult for me to make that kind of film ! And it was important for me to have a direct relationship with her, so that’s why I needed to operate the camera directly, and move around quickly.

In terms of crafting the performance, was it a challenge that there is almost no existing archival footage of Duse?

There was a recording by Edison, but that was lost. There were letters between her and her daughter Enrichetta [played here by Noémie Merlant]. Enrichetta was very religious, and her sons became priests. As for Valeria creating Eleonora, for me it was about finding her spirit. I wasn’t interested in the rise to fame; I was interested in the last few years when she was vulnerable and fragile, and also there was the dissolution of the country. That’s the situation that I wanted to depict.

In movies, people always want to see victories, but I wasn’t interested in that. I was much more interested in the failures. I’m very interested in the losers in history. The story of Duse shows how she was a revolutionary in theater, she was a real innovator. And many of her productions were not accepted by the public.

Early in the film , Eleonora wants to hold on to tradition, performing Ibsen and other staples of classic drama, and she resists the pull of modernity. But then there is a key encounter with Sarah Bernhardt, who accuses her of not keeping up with the new reality of the world after the war. That encounter shakes her to her core, and she then decides that she needs a wholly different approach.

There’s a human fragility that is innate in everyone, which is what I wanted to depict. Duse was modern, even in the beginning, but Italian theater was not. Sarah Bernhardt gave her that criticism. And that’s why she fell into the hands of this aspiring modern playwright, Giacomo Rossetti Dubois, who is not actually very good. But Eleonora wanted to be modern. She gave Giacomo a chance because she was trying to innovate. Sometimes artists create false myths. They believe in someone who turns out not to be so great. She thought that because he was young, he must be the future, he must be modern, but that wasn’t the case. And I wanted to show the delusion that she experienced by believing in this man who did not deserve her trust.

And what about the crisis in confidence she had after that meeting with Sarah Bernhardt?

She stopped acting, for many years. But when she needed the money, she went back to acting.

That’s an important theme in this film —what people do for money and for political accommodation. Eleonora is tempted to give in to Mussolini and accept his sponsorship, in order to support herself and her family.

When she went to meet with Mussolini, her objective was to raise money to build an innovative theater, but that wasn’t his intention. He wanted to own and possess her, because she was a great talent. Because she was fragile at that time, she almost fell prey to Mussolini and the rising fascism in Italy.

She was being neglected at this point in her career, because of her ties to the past. She became disillusioned. It was a decadent time, and everything was decomposing. There’s a parallel journey between her and the soldiers who had fallen in the war. The mothers had to cry for the men they lost.

We have a lot of monuments from after the First World War, dedicated to soldiers that died anonymously. Those statues were created to oppose the generals who created the war. But Mussolini wanted to own those as well. So the fascists turned these monuments to peace into pro-war symbols, in Africa and other colonies.

That’s happening now in the United States; the Department of Defense has become the Department of War. Everything is being turned around. The archival footage of the crowds greeting the trains carrying the unknown soldiers—was that originally in color?

No. It’s footage that was restored by the Cineteca di Bologna. I added the three layers of color, like an early Technicolor film . I’m an archivist; I love to work with archival footage. It is more powerful than fiction—it’s above fiction.

What has it been like making the switch from your early documentary work to these ambitious period films?

Duse has much in common with Martin Eden . I’m fascinated by people in revolt. The rebels. It’s the same story; Duse was a rebel for her time. She lived in a male-dominated world and at that time women were mostly in passive roles, and thanks to her things changed. Her talent was above the norm; it was larger than life. It was like a bomb, something monstrous.

The look of your film and the story, about a theater troupe in the period between the wars, made me think of the Soviet movie A Slave of Love (1976), by Nikita Mikhalkov.

That’s very interesting. Of course Eleonora was a woman of theater, and, as Robert Bresson said, cinema and theater are always in conflict. Slave of Love is a film ; it’s not theater. When you make a movie about theater, you’re still making a film . That creates a tension between the two art forms. Cinema became the modern art form. Theater is an older form, and that tension is very important to the film . Cinema can take characters from theater and put them in film . But you cannot have both.

Well, good movies are different from theater.

I try to do what I can [ laughs] . It’s complicated for me because of my judgment of myself.

How did you create the theater pieces? The staging of the productions?

I always use the pacing of cinema; it was never pure theater. This is a lesson I learned from the great masters of cinema. You should never bring theater into film and make them cohabitate. It’s always about maintaining the timing of cinema. Like The Golden Coach (1952) by Renoir, and Children of Paradise (1945) [by Carné], it’s cinema by way of theater.

What did playing the role do for Valeria? If you’re playing an actress, you must be thinking about your own work.

She had a fully fledged conversion. She changed a lot. This is a movie that changed her profoundly, especially because her approach was moral. She entered this character in a moral way. She had to bring a lot of herself to the role, as well as the character. She used to talk to Eleonora; she had a direct spiritual connection to her. It was very powerful and overwhelming. It was amazing to watch.

Her flow was uninterrupted. I let it go for 10 minutes at a time. I wanted this flow to go on and on. It was important for her to act without stopping the camera. I was possessed by Valeria, Valeria was possessed by Eleonora, and we had this powerful connection.

article_text:
埼玉県飯能市にある現代美術館「HYPER MUSEUM HANNO（ハイパーミュージアム飯能）」 （館⾧：後藤繁雄）で11月14日（土）から、生成AIアートの国際的なシーンを牽引し、世界的に高い評価を得るアーティスト、草野絵美さん（1990-）の大型美術館個展「エンド・オブ・ ノスタルジア」が開かれます。

本展は、TVモニターを積み上げた巨大なインスタレーション《Memory Metabolism》や立体作品《Mementoid》、プリント作品《Ornament Survival: Future Remains》などの新作を中心に構成されます。さらに世界最大級の現代アートフェアであるアートバーゼルなどで絶賛される《Ornament Survival》シリーズから、未発表作品を含むプリント約25点を展示。展示会場がひとつのインスタレーションとして現れ、まるで作品の世界に入り込んだかのようなアート体験ができます。

1990年に東京に生まれた草野さんは、自分が生まれる前の時代も含む「ありえたかもしれない過去・記憶」を、AIと協働して作品化。竹の子族、ギャル、デコラ（1990年代の原宿で生まれた 派手な色使いの服や、全身に過剰なまでにアクセサリーを身につけることが特徴 ）、ゴシック・ロリータなど、時代を横断する日本のストリート カルチャーを手がかりに、イメージの生成・選択・編集を重ねています。《Ornament Survival》では、自身の顔や身体を学習させたAIモデルを用い、自らの分身にさまざまな社会的役割や人物像を演じさせています。

そこでは忠実な再現よりも「違和感」「居心地の悪さ」が重視され、草野さんは自身の文化や経験をAIの表現に持ち込むことを「同質化していく世界に対する、アーティストとしての私のささやかな抵抗であり、遊び」と捉えています。 草野さんが見つめるのは、情報や関心が細分化されていくネット社会。かつて多くの人々が共有していた物語や時代の「記憶」は、これからどのように変わっていくのでしょうか――。ノスタルジアを喚起する基盤の揺らぎの中で、草野さんは「ありえたかもしれない記憶」を未来に向けて生成します。

article_text:
Tom Cruise will be the 52nd recipient of the American Film Institute ‘s prestigious life achievement award. The “Mission: Impossible” and “Digger” star will be feted with a gala tribute at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles on April 24.

“Tom Cruise is a global icon,” said AFI board of trustees chair Kathleen Kennedy wrote in a statement. “As an actor and producer, he brings an extraordinary commitment to everything he does. What I especially admire is his deep belief in movies and their ability to bring people together. That passion has made him an extraordinary ambassador for American film around the world. It is AFI’s honor to present him with the 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award.”

Now 64 years old, Cruise has remained one of the industry’s most prominent stars since he launched in the 1980’s with leading roles in “Risky Business,” “Top Gun,” and “The Color of Money.” As the unshakably determined secret agent Ethan Hunt, he led the “Mission: Impossible” action series across 30 years, starring in eight entries and subjecting himself to increasingly daredevil stunt-work as they went along. Other blockbuster titles have included “Rain Man,” “A Few Good Men,” “Collateral,” “Edge of Tomorrow,” and “Interview with the Vampire.”

Cruise has also been nominated for three Oscars: in lead actor for 1989’s “Born on the Fourth of July” and 1996’s “Jerry Maguire,” and in supporting actor for 1999’s “Magnolia.” He was also an Academy Award nominee as a producer for 2022’s “Top Gun: Maverick,” which was nominated for best picture. In 2025, he received an honorary Oscar from the Academy at the organization’s annual Governor’s Awards.

The star also finds himself back in the awards conversation this year for his lead turn in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s “Digger.” Cruise will next be seen in the sequel “Days of Thunder 2.”

The Life Achievement Award is AFI’s highest honor recognizing a career in the film industry. John Ford was the first recipient in 1973, with other notable names including Orson Welles, Alfred Hitchcock, James Stewart, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jack Lemmon, Tom Hanks, Robert De Niro, Meryl Streep, Jane Fonda, and Diane Keaton. More recent honorees include Julia Andrews, Nicole Kidman, and Francis Ford Coppola.

This year’s ceremony honored Eddie Murphy , with a recording of the tribute later premiering on Netflix. The event included Bill Burr, Dave Chappelle, Arsenio Hall, Spike Lee, Mike Myers, Chris Rock, and Stevie Wonder among its presenters and performers.
excerpt_original: The "Digger" and "Mission: Impossible" star will be at the center of a gala tribute in Los Angeles in April.

ホーム > 作品情報 > 映画「リアリティ・プラス」

リアリティ・プラス

劇場公開日： 2026年10月23日

解説・あらすじ

デミ・ムーア主演による世界的ヒット作「サブスタンス」で注目を集めたフランス出身のコラリー・ファルジャ監督が、同作の前身として2014年に手がけた短編SFロマンス。1日12時間だけ理想の自分になれるチップを埋めた男が見せかけの恋に翻弄される姿を通し、作られた美に依存し本物の自分を見失っていく現代社会の危うさを鋭く描き出す。 近未来のパリ。自分の容姿に強いコンプレックスを抱える青年ヴァンサンは、最新の脳内インプラント「リアリティ・プラス」を頭部に埋め込む。このチップを起動すると、デジタル技術により理想通りの完璧な容姿に変化し、周囲のユーザーからもその姿で見られるようになる。理想の身体を手に入れ自信に満ちあふれたヴァンサンは、同じくインプラントを使用している美しい女性ステラと出会い、瞬く間に恋に落ちる。しかしこの魔法のようなテクノロジーには、1日12時間しか作動しないという制限があった。 世界各地で製作された15～25分のショート映画を上映する企画「20分シネマ」の1作として劇場上映（2026年10月23日～10月29日、ヒューマントラストシネマ渋谷）。

2014年製作／22分／G／フランス 原題または英題：Reality+ 配給：SAMANSA 劇場公開日：2026年10月23日

『サブスタンス』の前身ということで、20分だし、他作のついでに鑑賞。 正直、設定にはかなり粗さを感じる。 まず「理想通りの容姿」ってことだけど、顔はキャラ選択みたいな感じでしかなかった。 体型は細かくいじれたものの、あれじゃ触れたつもりが届いてなかったりとかなるよね。 他キャラは不明だけど、主人公服も変わってたし。 それにあの仕組みだと、相手が時間切れになったら自分の見た目も戻っちゃう。 そもそもお互い偽の外見と分かってたら、一夜の夢にはよくても真剣交際になるかな？ とか諸々は一旦スルーして。笑 尺が短いからヒロインは即発情、最初のデートでチップに不具合と話はかなりサクサク進む。 そこに24時間起動可能になる違法処置の話が出てきて… ここの夢オチ部分は確かに『サブスタンス』的な要素を感じました。 オチは意外にも優しく可愛らしいものでしたが、それはそれで嫌いじゃないです。 しかし職場の同僚はよくお互い認識できたな。 あとヒロインちゃんは元の姿の方が断然好みなので、あんなもの使わずそのまま生きて下さい。 まぁクラブのシーンを見ても人の好みはそれぞれか。（特にバーテン）

article_text:
T here’s over-the-top … and there’s this playfully bizarre new film from US indie film-maker and genre connoisseur Anna Biller, whose previous film The Love Witch first alerted me to her ecstatic love of style, surface and the A-pleasures of the B-movie. The Face of Horror is a deadpan homage to the garish Technicolor horror pictures of Britain’s Hammer Films in the Peter Cushing 1960s, with an extraordinary visual emphasis on red velvet, whose Freudian significance can only be guessed at. Perhaps it’s not accurate to call it pastiche – in any event, the advent of AI has arguably undermined the value of skilled pastiche in movies and literature. It is more an attempt simply to make another film in the same vein as Hammer, to continue in the same rackety tradition of melodrama, eroticism and black comedy – and to create a film that can be laughed at as well as laughed with, just as they were at the time.

The setting is a cod-medieval England, a land of courtly nobles, smudgy-faced peasants and ladies wearing floor-length gowns with rope-style belts – although Biller has taken as her starting point the classic Japanese ghost story Yotsuya Kaidan, which is also an inspiration to, among others, Takashi Miike and Hideo Nakata . Edward (Jonah Hauer-King) is a handsome, unscrupulous knight, suspected of robbing his former master, seen here in the opening scene riding through a sun-dappled forest with his similarly shifty squire Richard (Leo Suter). Edward wishes to marry the blond, beauteous Eleanor (Kristine Froseth), who appears in a separate scene demurely preparing a preposterously lavish meal with her equally blond sister Beatrice (Ellie Bamber) in one of the vast, oppressive wood-panelled halls that Hammer horror was known for.

Edward and Richard brutally murder the women’s father and brother, who disapprove of them – blaming their death on “brigands” – and then marry Eleanor and Beatrice. But it isn’t long before the caddish Edward has designs on another evilly smiling noblewoman, Lady Isabel (Bella Heathcote), whose court of lute-strumming, recorder-blowing ladies-in-waiting is pictured in the vivid colour of a Ladybird book illustration from the same era as Hammer. They plot murderously against poor Eleanor, who has become the sickly, exhausted mother to Edward’s infant son. (The child is rather forgotten about here, but Biller may want to bring him back in adult form for a sequel.) It is to lead to the horror of supernatural revenge.

The most uproarious part of the film is the memento mori Danse Macabre scene at Lady Isabel’s decadent court, something that Ken Russell might have enjoyed – or Roger Corman, whose version of Poe’s The Masque of the Red Death may be an influence on Biller. The stamina and consistency of tone is what makes the film amusing and fascinating – a cult midnight movie of the future.

title_original: Kim Kardashian’s First Auction Purchase Was a Monet Painting Because of the Film ‘Clueless’
editorial_title_zh: 金·卡戴珊的首次拍卖购藏是一幅莫奈画作，原因竟是电影《独领风骚》
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位 Skims 创始人向乔纳森·范·梅特透露，在这本授权传记中，她买这幅画时超出了预算。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在乔纳森·范·梅特（Jonathan Van Meter）为金·卡戴珊（Kim Kardashian）撰写的传记《公民金》（Citizen Kim）中，作者透露这位亿万富翁真人秀明星兼 Skims 创始人拥有一幅克劳德·莫奈（Claude Monet）的画作。", "links": [{"text": "Kim Kardashian", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/kim-kardashian/"}, {"text": "Monet", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/monet/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《好莱坞报道》发表的一段节选写道，范·梅特写道，卡戴珊买下这幅莫奈是因为 1995 年由艾丽西亚·希尔维斯通主演的电影《独领风骚》。“金买下一幅莫奈，并不是因为她曾参观过巴黎橘园美术馆著名的《睡莲》，也不是在艺术界人士坎耶·韦斯特的指导下，”范·梅特写道。", "links": [{"text": "The Hollywood Reporter ,", "url": "https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/arts/citizen-kim-book-excerpt-kim-kardashian-clueless-monet-1236736291/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《独领风骚》上映时卡戴珊 14 岁，她曾称这是她最喜欢的电影之一。希尔维斯通饰演的角色雪儿·霍洛维茨是一个精明诉讼律师的女儿，这很像卡戴珊已故的父亲、律师罗伯特·卡戴珊。雪儿最著名的台词之一是“她简直是个‘莫奈’。就像一幅画，懂吗？远看还行，近看却是一团糟。”卡戴珊告诉范·梅特，这句台词是“我买莫奈的原因。我买的第一件真正的艺术品——靠我自己——就是莫奈。因为在电影里，如果女孩远看好看，但近看只是一团糟，他们就会称她们为‘莫奈’。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这本书中，卡戴珊说她在罗马与芬迪前女装艺术总监金·琼斯（Kim Jones）一起参加拍卖会时买下了这幅画，琼斯曾与她合作过 Fendi x Skims 系列。“我真的很想要这幅莫奈画作，因为这是一幅灰色的莫奈——一处美丽的风景，但却是灰色的……我真的很想把它放在我在棕榈泉的安藤忠雄（Tadao Ando）设计的房子里，那里全是混凝土。我在不断竞标，而且这是我经历过的第一次拍卖，所以我真的不知道它们是如何运作的，”卡戴珊告诉范·梅特。“但你真的会全身心投入进去。所以金·琼斯和我在一起，他说：‘拿下它！’所以我出价了。我赢了。而且我超出了我的预算，因为你当时正处于那种情境中。”Fendi x Skims 合作系列于 2021 年宣布，这表明这幅莫奈画作大约是在那个时候购入的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在 2020 年接受 E! 采访时，卡戴珊表示她收到过的最好的礼物是一幅卢西奥·丰塔纳（Lucio Fontana）的画作。在 2022 年《Vogue》对其住所的参观视频中，人们可以在她家的壁炉上方看到一块白色的丰塔纳画布。", "links": [{"text": "E!", "url": "https://www.eonline.com/photos/31657/everything-you-dont-know-about-kim-kardashian"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
In Citizen Kim , Jonathan Van Meter’s biography of Kim Kardashian , the author reveals that the billionaire reality TV star and Skims founder owns a painting by Claude Monet .

In an excerpt published by The Hollywood Reporter , Van Meter writes that Kardashian bought the Monet because of Clueless , the 1995 film starring Alicia Silverstone. “Kim bought a Monet not because she had visited the famous Water Lilies at l’Orangerie in Paris or under the art world tutelage of Kanye West,” Van Meter writes.

Clueless was released when Kardashian was 14, and she has called it one of her favorite films. Silverstone’s character, Cher Horowitz, is the daughter of a hard-nosed litigator, much like Kardashian’s late father, the attorney Robert Kardashian. One of Cher’s best-known lines is “She’s a full-on Monet. It’s like a painting, see? From far away it’s OK, but up close it’s a big ol’ mess.” Kardashian told Van Meter that the line is “the reason I bought my Monet. The first real piece of art that I bought—myself—was a Monet. Because in the movie they called the girls ‘a Monet’ if they look good from afar, but up close they’re just a mess.”

In the book, Kardashian says she bought the painting at auction while she was in Rome with Kim Jones, Fendi’s former artistic director of womenswear, who worked with her on a Fendi x Skims collection. “I really wanted this Monet painting because it’s a gray Monet—a pretty landscape, but gray. … I really wanted it for my Tadao Ando house in Palm Springs, which is all concrete. And I’m bidding and I’m bidding, and it was the first auction that I ever did, so I didn’t really know how they worked,” Kardashian told Van Meter. “But you get really into it. So Kim Jones is there with me and he’s like, ‘GET IT!’ So I bid on it. I win. And I went over what my budget was because you’re in the moment.” The Fendi x Skims collaboration was announced in 2021, which suggests that the Monet was bought around that time.

In a 2020 interview with E! , Kardashian says that the best gift she’s ever received is a Lucio Fontana painting. A white Fontana canvas can be seen above a fireplace in a 2022 Vogue tour of her home.
excerpt_original: The Skims founder tells Jonathan Van Meter in the authorized biography that she went over budget for the painting.

"translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览的第二章展出了 1997 年至 2012 年间的 6 幅横幅，以及 2023 年创作的 12 件 rontek（“小横幅”）。《夺回人民建立人民文化的权利》（Rebut Kembali Hak Rakyat Atas Pengembangan Kebudayaan 日，她与苏哈托一同被宣布为印度尼西亚国家英雄，许多人冷嘲热讽地认为这是普拉博沃政府为了争取工会支持而导演的一场政治噱头。通过 Taring Padi 的视角，您能跟我们多讲讲马尔西纳吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们将日惹工作室的展览空间命名为 Bilik "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "TARING PADI 的“Rakyat Pasti Menang”展览现场，伦敦 Ibraaz，2026 年。摄影：奥利·哈米克（Ollie Hammick）。图片由艺术家与 Ibraaz 提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "您能跟我们多讲讲《夺回人民建立人民文化的权利》（Rebut Kembali Hak Rakyat Atas Pengembangan Kebudayaan Rakyat）这件作品吗？你们是如何开始与德朗古（Delanggu）的这个社群合作的？这幅横幅是在什么场合展出的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是我们最早的大型横幅之一，创作于 1999 年，是中爪哇德朗古（Delanggu）举办的 Festival Memedi Sawah（“稻草人节”）的一部分，德朗古距离我们的工作室有两小时车程。它是为了开展反对农药的竞选活动、倡导传统和有机耕作方法而制作的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一切始于 1999 年 10 月在日惹有机农产品商店 Sahani 的开业活动上，当时我们制作了带有“反对化学农药”标语的硬纸板木偶。三个月后，我们发现自己和德朗古的 Kranggan 村青年组织以及环保非政府组织 Keliling 一同生活和工作。在开展一日文化活动期间，这面横幅被挂在村里的足球场上充当舞台背景。此前，我们举办了一场稻草人比赛，邀请农民和艺术家共同创作稻草人。自那时起，Taring Padi 便延续了这种合作且极具社会参与感的工作方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "TARING PADI 在伦敦 Ibraaz 的展览“Rakyat Pasti Menang”，2026 年。摄影：Ollie Hammick。图片由艺术家与 Ibraaz 提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览展出了你们最早的两幅木刻作品。Taring Padi 是如何开始涉足木刻创作的，尤其是此处展出的三件大型作品？随着这一新媒介的引入，Taring Padi 的艺术语言是如何演变的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "木刻横幅双联画《Buruh Bersatu》（工人联合）与《Tanah & Petani Merdeka Menghidupi Semua》（农民养育所有人，两件均创作于 2003 年）是我们首次采用木刻技法共同创作的作品。《Naikkan Upah Buruh》（提高工人工资）则由我们的一位成员于 2008 年制作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "木刻海报（通常为 A3 或 A4 规格）一般是独立创作的。每位成员会针对某个主题——例如油价上涨或大选——发展出自己的诠释，然后将其作为集体创作的一部分提交，且不署名。每当我们决定制作大型木刻作品（例如本次展览第二章中展出的这些）时，我们会共同完成。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们的视觉语言在三大主要媒介——木刻版画、硬纸板木偶和大型横幅——中同步且均等地演变。你会发现相同的图解和人物在所有三者中反复出现，其中包括玛丝娜（Marsinah）的形象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为一名艺术史学家，我能看出 Taring Padi 的视觉语言始终是由主题、政治以及我们合作的群体所决定的，而不是相反。我们的视觉共同语正是这一过程的产物——我甚至认为，这一过程塑造了每一位成员各自的视觉词汇。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_9-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_10.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "TARING PADI 在伦敦 Ibraaz 的展览“Rakyat Pasti Menang”布展现场，2026 年。摄影：Ollie Hammick。图片由艺术家与 Ibraaz 提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些作品中是否有哪件是应某些组织（例如工会）的专门委任而创作的？如果是的话，能否谈谈合作的过程？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一件都没有。不过，我们接受过最早的委任是在 1999 年，来自雅加达的国家反对对妇女暴力委员会。他们给我们提供了一个特定主题——一段简短的说明文字——然后我们便制作了横幅。最初的事情就是这么简单。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们为稻草人节制作的横幅《Rebut Kembali》出于我们的自愿，但整个创作过程仍然是合作性的。我们与村民们讨论了横幅中需要探讨的议题，并根据这些对话展开创作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自从我们在文献展第 15 届（Documenta 15）之后开始更多地开展国际化合作以来，这种情况发生了很大变化。第三章将展出这一时期的横幅。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你们与工会的合作在国际舞台上是如何发展的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在过去四年里，我们的国际知名度显著提升。在文献展第 15 届（Documenta 15）之后，我们在阿姆斯特丹、布里斯班和威尼斯举办了个人展览；我们现已受邀参加 2027 年横滨三年展。老牌艺术机构也开始收藏我们的作品，其中包括珀斯的西澳大利亚美术馆和伦敦的泰特现代美术馆。这种机构层面的青睐——我不想说它是“危险的”——但它实在是太诱人了！", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们应对曝光度增加的策略之一就是与工会合作。我给你们讲个故事。去年（2025 年），我们与意大利总工会（CGIL）合作，具体是与其位于罗马的针对外来务工人员的分支机构（FLAI）合作。我们创作了一幅关于在罗马周边农业种植园工作的印度锡克教客工的横幅。我们走访了他们的住所、寺庙，和他们一起吃喝。这幅名为《Basta Schiavitu》（停止奴役）的横幅在罗马的 Cantadora 画廊展出。CGIL 表达了购买这幅横幅的意愿，但讨论最终无果而终。最后，这幅横幅留在了罗马，CGIL 在他们的政治行动和会议中将其用作背景，甚至在一场为一名在田间劳作死亡的工人进行的诉讼中也使用了它。我们很高兴我们的作品能够在这种背景下发挥作用，并且只要这幅横幅能够实现其作为政治工具的功能，我们对它留在罗马没有任何异议。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "去年4月，我们还参加了在沃特利庄园（Wortley Hall）举行的“抵抗中的文化”（Culture in Resistance）。这座位于南约克郡的18世纪宅邸于20世纪50年代被工会收购，如今作为工会和劳工运动活动人士的非营利合作场地运营。明年我们将与总部位于奥斯陆、致力于阿拉伯流散文化的机构 Masahat 以及挪威工会联合会合作，创作一幅关于外来务工人员的横幅。我们遵循这一轨迹，作为建立进步联盟目标的一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/SnapInsta.to_809039571_18648508471026534_6970915372018294021_n.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "TARING PADI 在伦敦 Ibraaz 的展览“Rakyat Pasti Menang”，2026 年。摄影：Ollie Hammick。图片由艺术家与 Ibraaz 提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在新千年初，我们经历了诸如 2001 年 9 月 11 日这样天翻地覆的事件，它开启了长达数十年的伊斯兰恐惧症以及美国发动的“反恐战争”，特别是在伊拉克和阿富汗。尽管地理位置遥远，但印尼长期以来与伊拉克一样，背负着西方企业掠夺性资源开采的诅咒，并且和阿富汗一样占据着关键的地缘政治地位。作为艺术家以及关注反帝的社会正义活动家，Taring Padi 当时是如何对“9·11”之后的局势做出反应的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们从阶级的视角来看待这一点：“反恐战争”是新帝国主义的一部分，其中军事力量与新自由主义经济政策一同使用，或作为其一部分。我们的回应体现在美国国旗和其他刻板形象作为对立元素出现在我们的作品中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们从未将其视为针对伊斯兰世界的战争，而是资本主义世界秩序的重新划分。大规模森林砍伐和棕榈油产业从2002年起成为印度尼西亚经济的重要支柱，这绝非巧合。同样并非巧合的是，正是在同一时期，我们越来越多地开始与环保和原住民群体合作。这也是印尼寡头巩固其权力和与政府勾结的时期。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_3-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2026年，TARING PADI 在伦敦 Ibraaz 举办的“Rakyat Pasti Menang”展览现场。摄影：Ollie Hammick。图片由艺术家和 Ibraaz 提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2012年出版《Art Smashing Tyranny》时，你曾写到观点和背景的多样性，“特别是年轻一代，如今已成为 Taring Padi 活动背后的推动力”。你会如何总体描述这代年轻人的心态？在此期间，Taring Padi 大约有多少成员？从1997年到2010年代初，你们的艺术方向以及工作方法是如何演变或改变的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "年轻一代对抗军事独裁斗争的经历与第一代人有所不同。然而，我们在“艺术实践应参与社会政治变革”这一点上有着共同的看法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "关于他们的心态，值得注意的是，年轻一代并不以艺术院校学生为主。这意味着“艺术”并非影响他们决定加入 Taring Padi 的主要条件，尽管他们最终会跟我们一起学习“艺术”。他们非艺术专业的背景对我们的艺术方向作出了重大贡献。是的，他们从艺术院校的成员那里学习了光影和色彩技术，但也带来了不同的图案和风格。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当我们说“共同学习与工作”是我们的运作原则时，我们是在最字面的意义上践行这一点的。在我看来，团结是最核心的要素。正是在那时，“集体性”才在我们日常的动态中具体化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们没有确切的成员人数。成员身份是劳动导向的：你不断与 Taring Padi 一起工作，通过缓慢且有机的共同学习和工作过程，逐渐成为成员。目前我们有15名活跃成员，不过大家可以休息，并在想回来时随时回来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "叶真真（Chin-chin Yap）是一位常驻里斯本的新加坡作家兼电影人，也是 ArtAsiaPacific 的特约编辑。", "translated": true}]

Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Part II of our interview series with Taring Padi delves into the second chapter of the Indonesian collective’s exhibition “Rakyat Pasti Menang (The People United Will Never Be Defeated),” currently on view at Ibraaz London until October 18. In this conversation, Alexander Supartono—a first-generation member of Taring Padi and an associate professor at Edinburgh Napier University—tells ArtAsiaPacific about the works in the second chapter, which address land justice and workers’ rights. The interview about the first chapter of “Rakyat Pasti Menang” can be read here .", "links": [{"text": "here", "url": "https://www.artasiapacific.com/people/rakyat-pasti-menang-the-people-united-will-never-be-defeated-interview-with-taring-padi-part-1/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The second chapter of “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz features six banners and prints covering the period from 1997 to 2012. Can you tell us how Ibraaz and Taring Padi decided that this chapter should focus on land justice and workers’ rights? What were the main social and political agendas that Taring Padi was addressing with these works?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The decision simply came from observing our archive and looking at the topics we addressed frequently after the dust had settled following the 1998 Reformasi. We work extensively with laborers and peasant communities, as well as Indigenous groups. We don’t call ourselves artists but art workers. The association with and aspiration toward (as well as the idealization of) the working class is quite self-evident from this perspective, hence the recurrence of workers’ issues in our oeuvre."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Yogyakarta, where we are based, is largely agricultural compared to Jakarta. It’s also the second-most popular tourist destination in Indonesia after Bali. We’re surrounded by paddy fields and peasant communities who struggle to keep their land from being overrun by urbanization and the hospitality industry. This has played a role in the consistent presence of peasant iconography in our works."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_1-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Installation view of TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photo by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The struggle for environmental justice is mentioned in our manifesto, which translates into our alliance with, and support for, the rights of Indigenous people to their land. They also come to us and invite us to join their efforts, and we respond accordingly by producing works that address their specific hardships. The political and activist subject matter comes from them, and our role is to be part of their struggles by doing what we are good at."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The second chapter of the show displays six banners from 1997 to 2012 along with 12 rontek (“small banners”) from 2023. The Rebut Kembali Hak Rakyat Atas Pengembangan Kebudayaan Rakyat ( Reclaim People’s Right to Establish People’s Culture ) banner is from 1999 and was remade in 2022 for Documenta 15. Because of their function as political tools, our banners are often borrowed for various events. Some of them never return, particularly those borrowed between 1998 and 2002. Documenta 15 encouraged us to remake three of the lost banners, including Rebut Kembali . We also recreated two banners for our exhibition at Ibraaz. In this sense, we use exhibitions as a way to rebuild our archive."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Marsinah (1997–98) commemorates Indonesia’s most famous trade unionist, a 24-year-old woman who was kidnapped and tortured to death in 1993. Last year, on November 10, she was declared a National Hero of Indonesia alongside Suharto, which many cynically wrote off as a political stunt by the Prabowo administration to gain trade union support. Can you tell us more about Marsinah through Taring Padi’s eyes?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "We named the exhibition space in our Yogyakarta studio Bilik Marsinah (translated as “the Marsinah Room”), and she often appears in our works as a protagonist-figure. Suharto, meanwhile, is the most identifiable antagonist-figure in our work, representing the face of Indonesia’s military dictatorship. The regime’s interventions in workers’ rights disputes resulted, among many other incidents, in the brutal rape and murder of Marsinah in 1993."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "These two contrasting figures tell you how we felt when we learned that Marsinah and Suharto had been declared National Heroes on the same day last year. What is more ironic is that both families attended the inauguration ceremony: the victim’s and the perpetrator’s families were in the same room at the Indonesian Presidential Palace to receive the same accolade."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For Taring Padi, this political stunt by the Prabowo government confirms that we need to continue our struggle to support genuine workers’ movements in Indonesia and around the world."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_8-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_7-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Installation views of TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. How did you start working with this community in Delanggu and on what occasion was the banner displayed?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This is one of our earliest large-scale banners, created in 1999 as part of the Festival Memedi Sawah (“scarecrow festival”) in Delanggu, Central Java, which is a two-hour drive from our studio. It was made to campaign against pesticides and advocate for traditional and organic farming methods."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "It started when we made cardboard puppets with an “anti-chemical pesticide” message for the opening of Sahani, an organic farmers’ shop, in Yogyakarta in October 1999. Three months later, we found ourselves living and working together with a youth organization in Kranggan village in Delanggu and Keliling, an environmental NGO. The banner was displayed on the village football field as a stage backdrop during a day of cultural activities. This followed a scarecrow competition where we invited farmers and artists to create scarecrows together. Since then, Taring Padi has maintained this collaborative and socially engaging method of working."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/16/43/16435400-f27e-4b41-b5f7-d0c24f5ce4de/content/images/2026/10/Taring-Padi_Rakyat-Pasti-Menang_Ibraaz--courtesy-of-the-artist-and-Ibraaz--photo-Ollie-Hammick-_6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ArtAsiaPacific"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. People

Rakyat Pasti Menang (The People United Will Never Be Defeated): Interview with Taring Padi, Part II

TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photo by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

Part II of our interview series with Taring Padi delves into the second chapter of the Indonesian collective’s exhibition “Rakyat Pasti Menang (The People United Will Never Be Defeated),” currently on view at Ibraaz London until October 18. In this conversation, Alexander Supartono—a first-generation member of Taring Padi and an associate professor at Edinburgh Napier University—tells ArtAsiaPacific about the works in the second chapter, which address land justice and workers’ rights. The interview about the first chapter of “Rakyat Pasti Menang” can be read here .

The second chapter of “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz features six banners and prints covering the period from 1997 to 2012. Can you tell us how Ibraaz and Taring Padi decided that this chapter should focus on land justice and workers’ rights? What were the main social and political agendas that Taring Padi was addressing with these works?

The decision simply came from observing our archive and looking at the topics we addressed frequently after the dust had settled following the 1998 Reformasi. We work extensively with laborers and peasant communities, as well as Indigenous groups. We don’t call ourselves artists but art workers. The association with and aspiration toward (as well as the idealization of) the working class is quite self-evident from this perspective, hence the recurrence of workers’ issues in our oeuvre.

Yogyakarta, where we are based, is largely agricultural compared to Jakarta. It’s also the second-most popular tourist destination in Indonesia after Bali. We’re surrounded by paddy fields and peasant communities who struggle to keep their land from being overrun by urbanization and the hospitality industry. This has played a role in the consistent presence of peasant iconography in our works.

Installation view of TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photo by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

The struggle for environmental justice is mentioned in our manifesto, which translates into our alliance with, and support for, the rights of Indigenous people to their land. They also come to us and invite us to join their efforts, and we respond accordingly by producing works that address their specific hardships. The political and activist subject matter comes from them, and our role is to be part of their struggles by doing what we are good at.

The second chapter of the show displays six banners from 1997 to 2012 along with 12 rontek (“small banners”) from 2023. The Rebut Kembali Hak Rakyat Atas Pengembangan Kebudayaan Rakyat ( Reclaim People’s Right to Establish People’s Culture ) banner is from 1999 and was remade in 2022 for Documenta 15. Because of their function as political tools, our banners are often borrowed for various events. Some of them never return, particularly those borrowed between 1998 and 2002. Documenta 15 encouraged us to remake three of the lost banners, including Rebut Kembali . We also recreated two banners for our exhibition at Ibraaz. In this sense, we use exhibitions as a way to rebuild our archive.

Marsinah (1997–98) commemorates Indonesia’s most famous trade unionist, a 24-year-old woman who was kidnapped and tortured to death in 1993. Last year, on November 10, she was declared a National Hero of Indonesia alongside Suharto, which many cynically wrote off as a political stunt by the Prabowo administration to gain trade union support. Can you tell us more about Marsinah through Taring Padi’s eyes?

We named the exhibition space in our Yogyakarta studio Bilik Marsinah (translated as “the Marsinah Room”), and she often appears in our works as a protagonist-figure. Suharto, meanwhile, is the most identifiable antagonist-figure in our work, representing the face of Indonesia’s military dictatorship. The regime’s interventions in workers’ rights disputes resulted, among many other incidents, in the brutal rape and murder of Marsinah in 1993.

These two contrasting figures tell you how we felt when we learned that Marsinah and Suharto had been declared National Heroes on the same day last year. What is more ironic is that both families attended the inauguration ceremony: the victim’s and the perpetrator’s families were in the same room at the Indonesian Presidential Palace to receive the same accolade.

For Taring Padi, this political stunt by the Prabowo government confirms that we need to continue our struggle to support genuine workers’ movements in Indonesia and around the world.

Installation views of TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photos by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

Can you tell us more about Rebut Kembali Hak Rakyat Atas Pengembangan Kebudayaan Rakyat ? How did you start working with this community in Delanggu and on what occasion was the banner displayed?

This is one of our earliest large-scale banners, created in 1999 as part of the Festival Memedi Sawah (“scarecrow festival”) in Delanggu, Central Java, which is a two-hour drive from our studio. It was made to campaign against pesticides and advocate for traditional and organic farming methods.

It started when we made cardboard puppets with an “anti-chemical pesticide” message for the opening of Sahani, an organic farmers’ shop, in Yogyakarta in October 1999. Three months later, we found ourselves living and working together with a youth organization in Kranggan village in Delanggu and Keliling, an environmental NGO. The banner was displayed on the village football field as a stage backdrop during a day of cultural activities. This followed a scarecrow competition where we invited farmers and artists to create scarecrows together. Since then, Taring Padi has maintained this collaborative and socially engaging method of working.

TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photo by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

The exhibition features two of your first woodcuts. How did Taring Padi start working with woodcuts, in particular the three large-scale examples here? How did Taring Padi’s artistic language evolve with this new medium?

The woodcut banner diptych, Buruh Bersatu ( Workers United) and Tanah & Petani Merdeka Menghidupi Semua ( Farmers Give Life to All ) (both 2003), are the first works we made collaboratively using the woodcutting technique. Naikkan Upah Buruh (Raise Workers’ Wages) was made in 2008 by one of our members.

Woodcut posters (typically in A3 or A4 format) are usually produced individually. Each member develops their own interpretation of a topic—for example, the rise in petrol prices or a general election—and then submits it as part of the collective’s body of work, without their name being mentioned. From time to time, when we decide to make large-scale woodcuts, such as those on display in this exhibition’s second chapter, we make them together.

Our visual language has evolved simultaneously and equally across our three main mediums: woodcut prints, cardboard puppets, and large-scale banners. You will see the same iconography and characters recurring across all three, including the figure of Marsinah.

As an art historian, I can see that Taring Padi’s visual language has always been dictated by the topic, by politics, and by the communities we work with, rather than the other way around. Our pictorial commonplace is the result of this process—I would also argue that this process has shaped each individual member’s visual vocabulary.

Installation views of TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photos by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

Were any of these works specifically commissioned by organizations (e.g. trade unions), and if so, can you offer some insight into the collaboration process?

None of them. However, the earliest commission we received was in 1999 from the National Commission on Violence Against Women in Jakarta. They gave us a specific topic—a one-paragraph brief—and we made the banners. It was as simple as that in the beginning.

We made the banner for the scarecrow festival, Rebut Kembali , of our own volition, but the overall process was still collaborative. We discussed the issues that needed to be addressed in the banner with the villagers, and developed it from those conversations.

This changed considerably when we began working more internationally after Documenta 15. The third chapter will show banners from this period.

How has your work with trade unions developed in the international arena?

Our international profile has grown significantly in the past four years. After Documenta 15, we had solo shows in Amsterdam, Brisbane, and Venice; we’ve now been invited to participate in the 2027 Yokohama Triennale. Established art institutions have started to collect our works, including the Art Gallery of Western Australia in Perth and the Tate Modern in London. This kind of institutional patronage is—I don’t want to say “dangerous”—but it’s so seductive!

One of our strategies to deal with our increased visibility is to work with trade unions. I’ll tell you a story. Last year, in 2025, we worked with the Italian General Confederation of Labor (CGIL), specifically with the branch dealing with migrant workers in Rome (FLAI). We created a banner about Sikh migrant workers from India working in agricultural plantations around Rome. We visited their lodgings, their temples, we ate and drank with them. The banner, titled Basta Schiavitu (Stop Slavery) , was exhibited at Rome’s Cantadora gallery. CGIL expressed their intention to purchase the banner, but the discussion went nowhere. In the end, the banner stayed in Rome and CGIL used it as a backdrop in their political actions and meetings, even during a court action for one worker who died in the field. We were glad that our work was able to contribute in this context, and had no problem with the banner staying in Rome as long as it realized its function as a political tool.

Last April, we were also part of Culture in Resistance at Wortley Hall, an 18th-century mansion in South Yorkshire acquired by trade unions in the 1950s, which now operates as a nonprofit co-operative venue for trade union and labor movement activists. Next year we will work with Masahat, an Oslo-based organization dedicated to Arab diasporic culture, and the Norwegian Confederation of Trade Unions to create a banner about migrant workers. We follow this trajectory as part of our objective of establishing progressive alliances.

TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photo by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

At the start of the millennium, we experienced cataclysmic events such as September 11, 2001, which ushered in decades of Islamophobia and the US-led “war on terror,” particularly in Iraq and Afghanistan. Although geographically removed, Indonesia has long shared Iraq’s curse of Western conglomerates’ exploitative resource extraction and, like Afghanistan, occupies a critical geopolitical position. How did Taring Padi react to the post-9/11 developments as artists and as activists for social justice concerned with anti-imperialism?

We see this from the perspective of class: the “war on terror” is part of a new imperialism in which military force is used alongside or as part of neoliberal economic policy. Our responses materialized in the appearance of the American flag and other stereotypical figures as antagonistic elements in our works.

We never saw it as a war against the Islamic world, but rather as a remapping of the capitalist world order. It is hardly coincidental that massive deforestation and the palm oil industry became major pillars of the Indonesian economy from 2002 onward. It is also hardly coincidental that, during that same period, we increasingly began working with environmental and Indigenous groups. This was also a time when Indonesian oligarchs consolidated their power and their collusion with the government.

TARING PADI ’s “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz, London, 2026. Photo by Ollie Hammick. Courtesy the artists and Ibraaz.

When Art Smashing Tyranny was published in 2012, you wrote about the diversity of perspectives and backgrounds “particularly from the younger generation that is now the driving force behind Taring Padi’s activities.” How would you generally describe the mindset of this younger generation? Approximately how many members were there in Taring Padi during this period? How did your artistic direction as well as your method of working evolve or change from 1997 to the early 2010s?

The younger generation’s experiences of the struggle against military dictatorship are different from the first generation’s. However, we share the same view that artistic practice should be involved in sociopolitical change.

Regarding their mindset, it’s noticeable that the younger generations are not dominated by art school students. This means that “art” is not the main condition influencing their decision to join Taring Padi, although they eventually learn “art” with us. Their non-art backgrounds have contributed significantly to our artistic direction. Yes, they learned lighting and coloring techniques from the art school members, but they also brought different patterns and styles.

When we say “learning and working together” is our operational principle, we apply that in the most literal way. Togetherness is the most crucial element, in my opinion. That’s when “collectivity” materializes in our day-to-day dynamics.

We don’t have an exact number of members. Membership is labor-oriented: you keep working with Taring Padi, and you gradually become a member through a slow and organic process of learning and working together. At the moment, we have 15 active members, although people can take a break and return whenever they want.

Chin-chin Yap is a Singaporean writer and filmmaker based in Lisbon, and a contributing editor for ArtAsiaPacific.
